la:verb:vigilo.gloss: to watch through, spend in watching, do or make while watching
senses: to watch through, spend in watching, do or make while watching
to watch, remain awake, keep or be awake at night
la:verb:vigilo.html:
vĭgĭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[vigil].
Neutr., to watch, i. e. to be or keep awake at night, not to sleep, be wakeful (class.; syn. excubo).
Lit.: ad multam noctem vigilare,: de nocte,: proximā nocte,: usque ad lucem,: ad ipsum Mane, .—With a homogeneous object: in lectitando ... vigilias vigilare, Gell. N. A. praef. § 19.—Impers.: redeo si vigilatur et hic,.—Transf.: vigilat Troicus ignis,burns continually,; so, flamma,: lumina (of a light-house),.—Prov.
Hic vigilans somniat, i. e. builds castles in the air, ; cf.: num ille somniat Ea, quae vigilans voluit?.—
Qui imperata effecta reddat, non qui vigilans dormiat, who dreams with his eyes open, goes to sleep over a thing, ; cf.: et vigilans stertis,: vigilanti stertere naso,.—Impers. pass.: redeo, si vigilatur et hic,.—
Trop.
In gen., to be watchful, vigilant: vigilantes curae,: oculi vigilantes,.—
In partic., to keep watch over any thing, to be watchful or vigilant: vigilandum est semper: multae insidiae sunt bonis, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 138 Rib.): excubabo vigilaboque pro vobis,: vigila, Chrysippe, ne tuam causam deseras,: ut vivas, vigila,: studiis vigilare severis,to engage in,: janitor ad dantes vigilet,: Mars, vigila, an invocation to Mars at the breaking out of a war, acc. to .—
Act., to watch through, spend in watching, to do or make while watching (poet.): noctes vigilantur amarae,; so, vigilata nox,: ubi jam breviorque dies et mollior aetas, Quae vigilanda viris,: carmen vigilatum,: vigilati labores,: magia occulta noctibus vigilata,pursued by night,.—Hence,
vĭgĭlans, antis, P. a. (acc. to I. B. 2.), watchful, anxious, careful, vigilant: vigilantes et boni et fortes et misericordes,: vigilans et acutus tribunus plebis,: vigilans et industrius homo,, B, 1: sentiet in hac urbe esse consules vigilantis,.—Comp.: nemo paratior, vigilantior, compositior,.—Sup.: dux (Hannibal),, ext. 1.—Adv.: vĭgĭlanter, watchfully, carefully, vigilantly, .—Comp.: vigilantius,.—Sup.: vigilantissime,.—*
vĭ-gĭlātē, adv., for vigilanter, watchfully, vigilantly, .

la:num:viginti.html:
vīginti (or XX.), num. adj.
Sanscr. vicati; Gr. εἴκοσι; Boeot. ϝίκατι
,

la:verb:vigeo.gloss: to be vigorous or thriving; thrive, flourish
senses: to be vigorous or thriving; thrive, flourish
to be in honor, esteem or repute; prosper
la:verb:vigeo.html:
vĭgĕo, ēre, v. n.
Sanscr. ugras, mighty; Gr. ὑγιής, sound; cf. Lat. vegeo, vigil, augeo
,
to be lively or vigorous; to thrive, flourish, bloom; to be in honor, esteem, repute, etc. (class.; mostly of things, concrete and abstract; cf. valeo).
In gen.: quae a terrā stirpibus continentur, arte naturae vivunt et vigent,: quod sentit, quod sapit, quod vivit, quod viget,: sive occiderit animus sive vigeat,: vegetum ingenium in vivido pectore vigebat,: Volsci fessi ... Romani vigentes corporibus,: animus Laetitiā viget,: nos animo duntaxat vigemus, etiam magis quam cum florebamus,: memoriā vigere,: viget aetas, animus valet,: fama Mobilitate viget,: nec viget quicquam simile aut secundum,: cujus facta viva nunc vigent, Naev. ap : vigebant studia rei militaris,: audacia, largitio, avaritia vigebant,: tui politici libri omnes vigent, Cael. ap. : quem (Philonem) in Academiā maxime vigere audio, i. e. is in the highest repute or esteem, ; so ; : Harmodius in ore et Aristogito ... viget,: regum conciliis,.—
Of persons, to live, be alive: Persarum vigui rege beatior. ; : ab tergo Alpes urgent, vix integris vobis ac vigentibus transitae,.

la:adj:vigil.html:
vĭgil, ĭlis (
gen. plur. vigilium, ), adj.
vigeo
, awake, on the watch, alert (class.; cf.: insomnis, exsomnis).
Lit.
Adj.: prius orto Sole vigil calamum et chartas et scrinia posco,; : vigilum canum excubiae,: ales,i. e. the cock,: Aurora,: custodia, et saep.—Transf., of things, wakeful, watchful, etc.: oculi,: ignis,i. e. always burning,: lucernae,night-lamps,: auri vigili bibere,wakeful, listening,: nox,.—
Subst.: vĭgil, ĭlis, m., a watchman, sentinel: clamor a vigilibus fanique custodibus tollitur,; ; : nocturni,.—

Of such vigiles there were in Rome, from the time of Augustus, seven divisions, with their prefects and sub-prefects, constituting a regularly organized night-police, ; ; .—Transf., a sentinel: mundi (sol et luna), (1434).—Of cocks: nocturni,.—

Trop.: cura,wakeful, active,; : questus,uttered by night,.

vĭgor, ōris, m.
vigeo
,
liveliness, activity, force, vigor (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; not in Cæs. or Cic.): nec tarda senectus Debilitat vires animi mutatque vigorem,: igneus est ollis vigor, : juventas et patrius vigor,: animi,; : mentis,: quantum in illo (libro), di boni, vigoris est, quantum animi!: gemmae,strong brilliancy,; cf. . —Plur.: vigores mentium,: animorum,; .

vĭgōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
vigor

senses: a section of night-time, itself divided into four season-dependent vigiliae (the longer the night, the longer the vigilia)
la:noun:vigilia.html:
vĭgĭlĭa, ae, f. (
neutr. collat. form vĭgĭ-lĭum, Varr. ap. ) [vigil].
Lit.
In gen., wakefulness, sleeplessness, a lying awake: ut neque vigilia praecesserit neque ventris resolutio,: corporum robora nocturnā vigiliā minuere,: cui non sunt auditae Demosthenis vigiliae?; id. Par. prooem. § 5.—
In partic.
Lit., a keeping awake for the security of a place, esp. of a city or camp, a watching, watch, guard (cf.: excubiae, statio): noctu vigilias agere ad aedes sacras,: vestra tecta custodiis vigiliisque defendite,: exercitus stationibus vigiliisque fessus,: vigiles scutum in vigiliam ferre vetuit,to take on guard,: vigiliarum nocturnarum curam per urbem magistratibus mandavimus,.—
Transf.
A watch, i. e. the time of keeping watch by night, among the Romans a fourth part of the night: nox in quattuor vigilias dividitur, quae singulae trium horarum spatio supputantur,: primā vigiliā capite arma frequentes,; ; : cum puer tuus ad me secundā fere vigiliā venisset,: de tertiā vigiliā,: tertiā vigiliā,; : de quartā vigiliā,.—
The watch, i. e. those standing on guard, watchmen, sentinels: milites disponit, non certis spatiis intermissis sed perpetuis vigiliis stationibusque,; ; ; ; ; ; .—
A watching at religious festivals, nightly vigils: Cereris vigiliae,; .—
Trop., watchfulness, vigilance (the figure taken from military sentinels; perh. only in the foll. passages; whereas vigilantia is far more freq.): ut vacuum metu populum Romanum nostrā vigiliā et prospicientiā redderemus,; cf.: quasi in vigiliā quādam consulari ac senatoriā,: cupio jam vigiliam meam, Brute, tibi tradere: sed ita, ut ne desim constantiae meae, my post, i. e. my office, duty, .—Plur.: cum summis vigiliis aliquid perficere, prooem. § 1.

senses: to begin to bloom or flourish
la:verb:vigesco.html:
vĭgesco, gŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [vigeo], to become lively or vigorous; to thrive, to begin to flourish or bloom (class.): de niloque renata vigescere copia rerum,; : jam laeti studio pedes vigescunt,: vestrae tum arae, vestrae religiones viguerunt, vestra vis valuit,: diu legiones Caesaris viguerunt, nunc vigent Pansae, vigent Hirtii, etc.,: summis honoribus et multā eloquentiā,.

la:noun:vigilantia.html:
vĭgĭlantĭa, ae, f.
vigilans, from vigilo
,
wakefulness (class.).
Lit.: erat (Plinii) incredibile studium, summa vigilantia,.—Jocosely: fuit (Caninius) mirificā vigilantiā, qui suo toto consulatu somnum non viderit,.—More freq.,
Trop., watchful attention, watchfulness, vigilance (syn.: sedulitas, diligentia): Siciliam virtute istius et vigilantiā singulari ... tutam esse servatam,; ; ; ; ; .
